methodology_notes: Item 1 could go either way. All four give only "NOT VERIFIED", which is one value of a tri-state scheme and never shows a three-way outcome. I credited all four because the label is exactly the example vocabulary. A stricter judge could reject the bare labels in W and Z, or all four. Item 4 for X is marginal: only one defect carries a severity label. I credited it for the explicit "Most damaging defect" plus "HIGH", but a strict reading of "ranks its defects" could mark it absent. Item 5 is scored on the presence of corrected code blocks. W and Z fail it, while X and Y pass because they quote the original code and never replace it. Item 6 is scored on whether a text says how a clean axis was checked. W's "Verified aspects" bullets are conclusions, not methods, so I scored them absent.
